CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

dparser is an R port of John Plevyak’s DParser, a scannerless GLR parser / parser generator (Tomita algorithm). It is mostly C (the vendored DParser sources in src/) with a thin R layer in R/.

It is used in two ways:

  • From C (the main use): downstream packages (e.g. rxode2) put LinkingTo: dparser in DESCRIPTION, #include <dparser.h> (not <dparse.h>), and call DParser entry points that dparser exports with R_RegisterCCallable(). Breaking an exported C entry point or its signature breaks those packages.
  • From R: mkdparse() (port of make_dparser) turns a .g grammar into C parser tables; dparse() compiles a grammar on the fly into a temporary DLL and parses a file with an R callback. This path is mainly for grammar testing.

Imports: digest, methods. Depends: R (>= 3.3). License: BSD_3_clause.

Build and Development Commands

# Install
R CMD INSTALL .

# Document (roxygen2; NAMESPACE and man/ are generated)
Rscript -e "devtools::document()"

# Full test suite (most test files skip_on_cran(), so set NOT_CRAN)
find src -name "*.so" -o -name "*.o" | xargs rm -f 2>/dev/null; NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test()"

# Single test file (filter = file name without "test-" and ".R")
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test(filter='concurrent-dparse')"

# R CMD check
Rscript -e "devtools::check()"

There are no vignettes. Readme.Rmd renders Readme.md.

Architecture

R layer (R/)

  • R/dparser.R – package doc, .onLoad() (sets options dpaser.rm.named.parser.dll, dpaser.rm.unnamed.parser.dll, dparser.echo.compile; note the historical dpaser spelling, keep it), and the exported functions:
    • mkdparse() – grammar file -> C tables via .Call(cDparser, ...) (17 arguments).
    • dparse() – writes C from the dpRparse() template, builds it with R CMD SHLIB in tempdir(), dyn.load()s it, caches by the grammar’s digest md5, and returns a parser function (dparserFunction S4 class).
    • dpIncludeDir(), dpGetFile(), dpDefaultSkip(), dpReload(), gc.dparser() (unloads/removes generated DLLs), .dparsePtr().
    • refresh() (internal) sources build/refresh.R.
  • R/Rparse.R (dpRparse()) and R/version.R (dpVersion()) are written by build/refresh.R; R/Rparse.R embeds build/Rparse.c as a string. dpVersion() is currently stale relative to DESCRIPTION.

C layer (src/)

  • Vendored DParser sources: parse.c, scan.c, lr.c, lex.c, gram.c, grammar.g.c, write_tables.c, read_binary.c, dsymtab.c, util.c, mkdparse.c, version.c and their headers (d.h, dparse.h, gram.h, …). They were imported from upstream by build/refresh.R (asserts rewritten to error(), printf -> Rprintf, C++ guards added) and have since been patched in place (see NEWS.md: buf_read(), d_pass(), udparse(), reentrant reduce_one()/build_paths(), typed hash callbacks).
  • src/dparser.c – dparserPtr() (returns the function pointer table) and R_init_dparser(): the .Call registration table (_dparserPtr, cDparser, with hardcoded arities) plus the long list of R_RegisterCCallable("dparser", ...) exports.
  • src/rdparse.c – dparse_sexp() (parses a file and walks the tree, calling the R callback fn / skip_fn) and __freeP().
  • src/mkdparser.c – cDparser(), the mkdparse() backend.
  • src/dparser.h – the public header downstream packages include; declares the callables resolved via R_GetCCallable().
  • src/dparserPtr.h – typedef’d function-pointer interface for the .dparsePtr() route.
  • src/install.libs.R – copies the shared library and also installs every src/*.h into the package include/ directory (this is what dpIncludeDir() points to and what LinkingTo uses).
  • src/Makevars – PKG_CFLAGS = -DUSE_FREELISTS -DTRACK_PNODES.

Adding or changing an exported C function

Keep these in sync: the implementation, its declaration in src/dparser.h (and src/dparserPtr.h if it is part of the pointer table), the R_RegisterCCallable() line in R_init_dparser(), and a NEWS.md entry. Never change an existing exported signature (e.g. buf_read() keeps its int *len ABI) – downstream packages compiled against the old header would break.

Thread safety

dparse()/udparse() may be called from several threads, one D_Parser per thread (rxode2 does this). Do not introduce process-wide static or global mutable state in the parse path. The dparser.h entry points must be resolved on the main thread; error reporting and R callbacks call the R API, so they are main-thread only.

build/ (excluded from the tarball)

  • build/refresh.R – clones upstream DParser into src/dparser/ and regenerates the vendored sources, src/dparser.h, src/dparser.c, R/version.R, R/Rparse.R, and copies upstream .g tests into tests/testthat/.
  • Do not run refresh() / build/refresh.R casually: it overwrites the in-place fixes in the vendored C files and the hand-maintained src/dparser.c (e.g. dparserPtr()). Port fixes by hand instead.
  • build/Rparse.c – template for the C file dparse() compiles.

Tests (tests/testthat/)

  • test-dparser.R – for every *.test.g grammar: mkdparse() it, compile with sample_parser.c via R CMD SHLIB, parse each *.test.g.N input and compare against *.test.g.N.check. Optional *.flags files set mkdparse() options. Whole file is skip_on_cran() and skipped on Solaris/macOS.
  • test-concurrent-dparse.R + helper-concurrent.R + concurrent_parser.c – builds a pthread test parser and checks concurrent parses against a serial run (rxode2#1427, #33). skip_on_cran() and skip_on_os("windows").
  • test-arbitrary.R, test-envir.R, test-unlink.R – R-level dparse() behavior using tran.g, ansic.test.g, etc.
  • test-mem-*.R – regression notes for memory-safety fixes; they skip() and point to standalone C reproducers in tests/audit-reproducers/ (excluded from the build).
  • Several large .g test grammars are listed in .Rbuildignore to keep the tarball small; a new big fixture may need the same treatment.
  • tests/testthat.R sets R_TESTS="" before test_check().

CI (.github/workflows/)

  • R-CMD-check.yaml – macOS, Windows, Ubuntu (devel, release, oldrel-1) on push/PR.
  • test-coverage.yaml – covr -> codecov.
  • pkgdown.yaml – site at https://nlmixr2.github.io/dparser-R/.
  • rhub.yaml – manual rhub::rhub_check() (e.g. clang-asan, clang-ubsan) with NOT_CRAN=true so the concurrency tests run; keep that dparser-specific change when updating the file.

Code Style

  • R: follow the existing style in R/dparser.R; roxygen comments use ##'. Do not hand-edit NAMESPACE or man/; run devtools::document(). Shared roxygen text is in man-roxygen/.
  • C: use Rprintf/Rf_error/Rf_warning, never printf, exit(), or assert() (CRAN). Bound-check user-supplied indices and sizes; recent fixes were all missing-bound / NULL / overflow bugs.
  • ASCII only in new or edited text (R, C, roxygen, NEWS.md, this file): use --, ->, straight quotes. CRAN requirement. (Older NEWS.md entries still contain some Unicode; do not add more.)
  • NEWS.md: one # dparser <version> heading per version, bullets describing the fix and user-visible effect.

Release / CRAN Cautions

  • dparser sits under rxode2 and the rest of the nlmixr2 ecosystem; check reverse dependencies before release (revdep/ is ignored).
  • Release files: cran-comments.md, CRAN-SUBMISSION (both build-ignored). Bump Version: in DESCRIPTION.
  • Keep tests that compile code or spawn threads behind skip_on_cran().
  • Do not commit compiled objects (*.o, *.so, *.dll) or the src/dparser/ upstream clone.

CRAN tests: never assert on timing

  • Never put a wall-clock timing expectation in a test that can run on CRAN: no expect_lt()/expect_true() on Sys.time() differences, system.time(), proc.time(), bench/microbenchmark results, or any other elapsed-time threshold. CRAN check machines are shared and heavily loaded, so elapsed time there is random and a timing assertion fails at random. Example: nlmixr2plot test-model-diagram.R asserted a modelGraph() call took < 30 s; on CRAN it took 48.4 s and failed.
  • Test the result, not the speed. If a speed regression guard is really needed, put it only in a test that starts with skip_on_cran() (or the package’s own CRAN skip helper), and never in examples or vignettes.
  • Tests that take more than a few seconds should also skip on CRAN.
